model_annotation: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with the co-occurrence number for several methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, an additional method shown in purple with an unreadable/obscured legend label, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick labels at approximately \(10^{1}\), \(10^{2}\), and \(10^{3}\), spanning from a few units to a few thousand (four plotted x-positions appear around ~5, ~30, ~300, and ~3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)”, uses a linear scale, and ranges from roughly 38% to 66% with regularly spaced tick marks every 5 percentage points (40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65). The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, rising from about 38% at the smallest co-occurrence number to about 42% at the second point, then to about 44% at the third point, and remaining near 44% at the largest co-occurrence number. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, increasing from about 40% to about 43%, then to about 46%, and ending around 48%. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from about 43% to about 45%, then to about 46–47%, and ending around 49–50%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from about 44–45% to about 49%, then to about 54%, and ending around 56–57%. The purple series (legend label not legible) is a solid line with pentagon-like markers, increasing from about 44% to about 51%, then to about 53%, and ending around 55%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 51% to about 57%, then to about 62%, and ending around 66%.
